# How a model produces code, and why it can be wrong {#sec-how-models-produce-code}

*A plain, non-technical account of what a model is doing when it writes code.*

::: {.callout-note}
## Draft stub — planned contents
The assistant predicts plausible continuations rather than reasoning about correctness. This is what makes it fast and fluent, and it is also why it can produce code that runs and is wrong, or that invents things that do not exist. Motivates the verification habit without any mathematics, and sets up why this new layer, unlike a compiler, must be verified.
:::
